method: A leak rate is a gas throughput, the product of pressure and volume divided by time, so every unit reduces to the SI unit pascal cubic metre per second by one exact factor and no measurement enters. The basis is the standard atmosphere of exactly 101 325 Pa, the litre of 0.001 m³ and the minute of 60 s: mbar·L/s is 0.1 Pa·m³/s, Torr·L/s is (101 325/760) x 0.001 = 0.13332237 Pa·m³/s, a lusec is a thousandth of that, atm·cm³/s is 0.101325 Pa·m³/s, sccm (atm·cm³/min) is 0.00168875 Pa·m³/s and slm (atm·L/min) is 1.68875 Pa·m³/s. Results keep six significant digits, trailing zeros are trimmed and thousands are grouped; a magnitude below 1e-6 or from 1e12 up is written in exponential form. Zero is accepted because a joint can be tight; negative values are refused because a leak rate is a magnitude, and anything above 1e6 Pa·m³/s is outside the supported range. Typed input may carry grouping commas but not a unit. The units written with the atmosphere follow NIST's convention of an ideal gas at 101 325 Pa and 0 °C; some instruments quote sccm at 25 °C instead, which changes the molar flow but not the pV/t conversion between these units. All arithmetic runs in the browser and the page makes no network request.
